newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - API data seen neutral for oil market.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - API data seen neutral for oil market.

text.p: The American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly oil inventory this evening is expected to show a mixed bag of draws and builds, giving the data a neutral hue in a market pining for direction.

"These APIs are not going to have much of an effect unless there are extreme surprises," said Jeff Foose, trader with KCS Energy in New Jersey. "We are possibly going to need several weeks of APIs for any direction. The market tends lose volatility this time of year." The week's expected builds and draws were already priced into the market, dealers said.
For the week ended January 24, traders are expecting distillate stocks to have dropped 1.5 million to 3.5 million barrels, with the consensus pegging the draw at two million.
Analysts said refined product stocks will attract the most attention in the report due to a spate of refinery turnarounds creating uncertanty about heating oil and gasoline supply.

"People will pay more attention to gasoline and distillates since I think products are what stopped us going down more," said Smith Barney analyst John Saucer, noting recent oil price declines. Gasoline stocks are expected to have grown between 1.5 million to 4.5 million barrels.

The expectation of a distillate stock decline stems from those stocks (composed of heating oil and diesel) declining historically this time of year. Dealers also cited talk of distillate exports from the U.S. Gulf draining stocks.
While January is the traditionally the poorest period of gasoline demand, dealers expect a bevy of imports from Europe to boost gasoline stock levels as well.

A pick up in imports from the North Sea is expected to have increased crude stocks by 1.5 million to 3.5 million barrels. Crude demand is also expected to have deteriorated due to heavy seasonal maintenance by refiners cutting output.
Dealers expect refinery utilization rates to have dropped up to one percentage point after declining 0.8 percentage point to 89.9 percent for the week ended January 17.
